actions.action: Check whether the pot has a drainage hole
If no hole, move plant to a plastic nursery pot with drainage set inside the ceramic pot
Slide plant out and inspect roots
Trim rotted roots with clean scissors
Remove fully black or dead leaves at the base
Repot in fresh airy mix (potting soil with perlite or bark) in a slightly larger pot
Water only when top 1-2 inches dry, soak and drain fully
Move plant to a spot near a window with bright filtered light
If tips keep browning, use filtered or rainwater or let tap water sit overnight
Keep plant away from cold drafts and heat vents
If roots mostly mush, save firm healthy sections and repot those
Report back what the roots look like

reason: The answer names overwatering and root rot as the main cause, and its main advice (unpot, inspect, remove the rot, fix drainage and watering) matches the fix, with soil repotting as a reasonable alternative to water propagation and nothing likely to harm the plant.
